source.title: A short tour of operator learning theory: Convergence rates, statistical limits, and open questions

accepted.question_text: Suppose one learns a holomorphic operator by empirical risk minimization using a neural operator whose trainable component is a fully trainable network, with particular interest in the noiseless case. Can such fully trainable ERM schemes achieve sample-complexity rates faster than the Monte Carlo rate, rather than being limited to roughly n^{-1/2} behavior?

evidence.quote: Based on the results presented in §2, it is natural to ask whether faster-than-Monte Carlo rates are possible when considering ERM with fully trainable networks, especially in the absence of noise.

accepted.question_text: For empirical risk minimization in operator learning under statistical noise, Theorem 1 gives a nonparametric rate that is at best n^{-1/2}. Is this rate merely an artifact of the proof technique used in the statistical-learning analysis, or does it reflect a genuine minimax barrier for the noisy operator-learning problem?

evidence.quote: A remaining question is whether the nonparametric rate in Thm. 1 (which is at best n−1/2) is an artifact of the statistical learning analysis in the noisy setting, or a genuine minimax barrier.

accepted.question_text: Let K be a class of target operators and compare the noiseless minimax sampling width s_n(K)_X with the noisy statistical nonlinear sampling width s̃_n^η(K; σ)_X for operator learning. Can one obtain a sharp characterization of operator-learning minimax rates that explicitly tracks the noise level σ, analogous to the known noise-aware theory for classical function approximation?

evidence.quote: An open problem is to obtain a similar noise level aware characterization of minimax rates for operator learning.

accepted.question_text: Which classes of operators arising in scientific applications are both practically relevant and mathematically structured enough to admit algebraic minimax sample-complexity rates for operator learning?

evidence.quote: Another important challenge is to identify classes of operators that are practically relevant in scientific applications, but still enjoy algebraic minimax sample complexity.

accepted.question_text: For the holomorphic operator classes studied in Theorems 1 and 2, can one prove sharp bounds for the statistical nonlinear sampling n-width s̃_n^η(K; σ) in L^2_ϱ? In particular, can such bounds determine whether suitably noisy operator-learning problems for these holomorphic classes still allow faster-than-Monte Carlo rates?
accepted.context_brief: Sharp noisy widths for holomorphic classes

evidence.quote: First, can one prove sharp bounds on the statistical n-width s˜ηn (K;σ)L2ϱ (11) for K the holomorphic classes considered in Thms. 1–2? This will help clarify whether faster-than-Monte Carlo rates are possible or not under suitable statistical noise models.

accepted.question_text: Is empirical risk minimization minimax-optimal, in the sense of the noiseless sampling-width formulation, for operator classes beyond holomorphic ones? Examples singled out by the paper include infinitely Fréchet-differentiable operator classes and classes generated by specific parametric PDE problems.

evidence.quote: Moreover, is ERM optimal in the minimax sense of (8) for target classes beyond holomorphic operators? Other sets of interest could include C∞ operators or those arising from specific parametric PDE problems.

accepted.question_text: Beyond classical operator classes defined by regularity assumptions such as smoothness or holomorphy, can one develop and analyze architecture-oriented classes of target operators whose definition is tied to approximation by specific neural-operator architectures, and use them as a mathematically meaningful alternative foundation for operator-learning theory?

evidence.quote: In addition, as suggested by the results in §3, an interesting alternative could be to consider architecture-oriented operator classes, in contrast to those based on more classical regularity assumptions.

accepted.question_text: Consider the class K_FNO^α of operators that can be approximated efficiently at rate α by Fourier neural operators, and let β★ denote the optimal algebraic minimax-rate exponent for learning that class in L^2_ϱ. The paper proves bounds showing β★ is at most 1/2 and approaches 1/2 as α grows. Is the exponent 1/2 actually sharp for these FNO-based operator classes, or can the true optimal exponent exceed the currently known upper-bound heuristic?

evidence.quote: Thm. 5 shows that the optimal algebraic minimax rate exponent is asymptotically 1/2 as α → ∞. The gap between the upper and lower bound in (10) for finite α is likely due to the ERM proof technique for the lower bound. It is of interest to determine whether the exponent 1/2 is sharp or not.

accepted.question_text: For operator learning in L^2_ϱ, how can one further separate the minimax behavior of holomorphic classes H(b)∘ι from the architecture-based classes K_FNO^α? Concretely, can one either prove stronger lower bounds on the sampling widths of K_FNO^α or show that operators in H(b)∘ι are themselves well approximated by Fourier neural operators, thereby clarifying whether the two classes have genuinely different sample-complexity behavior?

evidence.quote: A further separation of the left-hand side would require lower bounds on sn(KαFNO)L2ϱ or showing that elements of H (b) ◦ ι are well approximated by FNOs.
